revolutionary-battles-1775-1776.works: Red and blue diamonds are easy to tell apart and the battle legend is only three lines. Each battle pop-up puts the name and date in big text at the top, so I can get the date without reading the long story, and circle 4 says 'Victor: Britain' in plain words.

findings.where: Q1 'Where did the war begin?', steps 2, 4 and 5: Massachusetts bookmark view, Revolutionary War Battles and Turning Points layers
findings.what: No town names on the map. I see a blue diamond next to circle 1, circle 2, and another blue diamond out on the coast. Which one is Lexington and which is Boston? I can't see a Boston diamond, so I'd click the coast one. For Measure I don't know where to put the ends.
findings.why: I can't find the Boston battle, so I can't get the siege dates without asking. Circle 2 sits right on top of it. Without names I can't measure Boston to Concord either.
findings.suggestion: At bookmark zoom, put short labels on the diamonds ('Lexington & Concord', 'Siege of Boston'), or put a Boston and Concord place label on the map. Move the turning-point circles a little to one side so they don't cover the diamonds. Or change the sheet to: 'Boston is under circle 2. Click circle 2 and use the arrows.'
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q1-bookmark.png (no Boston diamond showing, circle 2 on Boston, no town labels); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q1-lexington.png

findings.where: Q2 'Where was the fighting in 1775, and where in 1776?', step 1: zoomed-out views
findings.what: When I can see Quebec, the map stops at Virginia. When I can see South Carolina, Quebec is gone. The legend box also covers the top right.
findings.why: I don't know how far to zoom, and if I zoom out one more step the diamonds get tiny and pile up.
findings.suggestion: Add an 'All battles 1775–1776' bookmark set to the Quebec-to-Charleston extent with the legend closed. Or split the step: 'look at the north, then pan south'.
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--open.png (Quebec to Virginia); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-colony.png (Lake Champlain to Georgia, no Quebec); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-all.png

findings.where: Q2, step 3: Thirteen British Colonies / Colony Area layer, clicking inside a colony
findings.what: I clicked Virginia and nothing happened. I clicked New York and nothing happened. I thought the map was broken.
findings.why: The sheet says the click gives the name. It doesn't, so I'm stuck. The only names are the words on the map. 'Massachusetts' is written way up in Maine, far from the Boston diamonds, and the Lake Champlain diamonds have no colony name near them.
findings.suggestion: Turn on pop-ups for Colony Area with just the colony name. Or change the sheet to 'Read the colony's name written on the map.' Put the Massachusetts label nearer Boston.
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-colony.png and --q2-colony-ny.png: '(no pop-up opened)'; revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--open.png (Massachusetts label in Maine)

findings.where: Q2, step 2: Revolutionary War Battles, every diamond at the zoomed-out view
findings.what: About twenty diamonds and I have to click every one to see the year. At Boston it says '1 of 3' and at New York four red diamonds are stacked on each other.
findings.why: That's a lot of clicking and writing for me. I'll lose track of which ones I've done and run out of time.
findings.suggestion: Show the year on the map: a small '1775'/'1776' label on each diamond at this zoom, or a different outline for 1775 and 1776 battles explained in the legend.
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-bunkerhill.png ('1 of 3' at Boston); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q2-all.png (overlapping red diamonds at New York)

findings.where: Q3 'Why New York?', step 1: Map layers list
findings.what: The sheet says Key Port Cities is inside Revolutionary War Battlefields. I opened that and it isn't there.
findings.why: I'd think I'm in the wrong place and give up or ask.
findings.suggestion: Fix the sheet: 'In Map layers, turn on Key Port Cities in the American Revolution 1775-1781 (second from the top).'
findings.evidence: Map layers list: Key Port Cities is its own layer, between Turning Points and Revolutionary War Battles, not inside Revolutionary War Battlefields

findings.where: Q3, steps 3–4: Key Port Cities layer, zoomed-out view
findings.what: I can see the big anchors but there are no city names on the map. The sheet says don't click them, use the coast and the diamonds. The diamonds have battle names, not port names, so I can't tell which big anchor is which. But when you do click an anchor, it tells you the name (Stonington, CT).
findings.why: I can maybe guess New York, but not Philadelphia or the one in Virginia. I can't answer the question, and the sheet is telling me not to do the one thing that would work.
findings.suggestion: Change the sheet: 'Click each big anchor to read the port's name.' Better still, label the Major Port City symbols on the map (Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Norfolk, Charleston).
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q3-ports.png (no city labels); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q3-port.png pop-up: 'Stonington, CT'

findings.where: Q4 'How did 1776 end?', steps 2–5: New York/New Jersey zoom, Turning Points circles 4 and 5, battle diamonds
findings.what: I click circle 4 and it says '1 of 5'. I can't see diamonds for Fort Washington or Fort Lee, just two red ones nearby with no names. At circle 5 there's no blue diamond, only a red one a bit south, so I'd think that's Trenton and the British won. Trenton has no name on the map for measuring.
findings.why: The diamonds I need are hidden under the circles, so I'd click the wrong ones and write the wrong winner.
findings.suggestion: Move the turning-point circles slightly to one side so the diamonds show, and label Fort Washington, Fort Lee and Trenton at this zoom. Or say on the sheet: 'Fort Washington and Fort Lee are under circle 4, Trenton is under circle 5. Click the circle and use the arrows.' I'd check which battle the red diamond south of circle 5 is.
findings.evidence: revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q4-circles.png (no blue diamond near circle 5, red diamond just south); revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q4-circle4.png ('1 of 5')

findings.where: Legend, Turning Points entry (q1-bookmark and q4-circles views)
findings.what: The legend shows an empty circle with no words next to it.
findings.why: If I didn't read the sheet's 'Reading the map' bit, I wouldn't know the numbers mean the order things happened.
findings.suggestion: Give the legend symbol a label: 'Turning point (number = order it happened)'.
findings.evidence: Legend text 'Turning Points' with an unlabeled circle in revolutionary-battles-1775-1776--q1-bookmark.png

roads-trails-and-rails-west.works: The trails legend is short and every trail's pop-up has its name at the top. The railroad pop-up gives one clear answer ('Railroad in operation by: 1869'), and big city names like Kansas City and St. Louis help me find where the trails start.

findings.where: Q2 'How far, and how many?', step 2: Trails West, clicking the Oregon Trail where trails share the same path
findings.what: I clicked the Oregon Trail and it said Pony Express Trail, '1 of 4'. I'd just copy the Pony Express numbers.
findings.why: I'd write the wrong length and never find how many people went on the Oregon Trail.
findings.suggestion: On the sheet, say where to click: 'Click the Oregon Trail in Idaho or Oregon, where it runs on its own,' or 'If it says 1 of 4, use the arrows until you see Oregon Trail.' On the map, put the Oregon Trail first in the pop-up order where the trails overlap.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--q2-oregon.png: pop-up header 'Pony Express Trail', '1 of 4'

findings.where: Q1 step 3 and Q2 step 2: trail pop-up text
findings.what: The pop-up is one long paragraph. The distance is in kilometers first, then miles in brackets: '2897 kilometers (1,800 miles)'.
findings.why: I have to read the whole thing to find the start, end and length, and I'd probably write the first number, which is kilometers, on a sheet that wants miles.
findings.suggestion: Start each trail pop-up with short fact lines: 'Starts: … Ends: … Length: … miles. Travelers: about …', then the story. Put miles first.
findings.evidence: Pony Express pop-up text: 'more than 2897 kilometers (1,800 miles)'. I didn't see the Oregon pop-up and am guessing it's set out the same way.

findings.where: Q1 step 1, Q2 step 1, Q3 step 3: Trails West colors
findings.what: Oregon and California are both a sort of olive. Mormon Pioneer, Old Spanish and Pony Express all look dark. Along the Platte they run together and look like one fat dotted line.
findings.why: I can't match a line to the legend, so I can't follow one trail from end to end.
findings.suggestion: Give each trail a clearly different color (for example a bright green Oregon, a gold California, a blue Mormon Pioneer and a red Pony Express) and make the dots bigger.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--open.png legend swatches; roads-trails-and-rails-west--q3-indigenous.png (trails overlapping across Wyoming/Nebraska)

findings.where: Q2 steps 3–4: basemap labels for Independence and Portland
findings.what: I can see Kansas City but no Independence, and Seattle and San Francisco but no Portland.
findings.why: I don't know where to start and stop the Measure line.
findings.suggestion: Add a small labeled point for Independence, MO and Portland, OR (or for each trail's start and end town), or tell students to zoom in on northern Oregon to find Portland.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--open.png (no Portland label); roads-trails-and-rails-west--q2-oregon.png (Kansas City labeled, no Independence)

findings.where: Q3 'Whose land?', steps 2–4: Indigenous Territories layer, zoomed in on Wyoming/Nebraska
findings.what: Big see-through boxes on top of each other, so the colors mix. The shapes the trail goes through (the gray one, the yellow one) have no name I can see. The names I do see are far from the trail, and some I can't read or say: 'Oohenumpa', 'Sicangu', 'Tsėsthoe (Cheyenne)'. There's also a town called Cheyenne.
findings.why: I can't tell which nation's land the trail crosses, so I'd just write the two names nearest it and not know if they're right.
findings.suggestion: Give each territory a pop-up with its name, English name first (the own-language name can follow), and add that to the sheet ('click a shaded area to read its name'). Add outlines so overlapping shapes can be told apart. I'd check whether territory pop-ups already exist.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--q3-indigenous.png (labels 'Tsėsthoe (Cheyenne)', 'Oohenumpa', 'Sicangu' away from the trail; no label in the gray and yellow shapes the trail crosses)

findings.where: Q4 'From trails to rails', step 2: Railroads on, opening zoom
findings.what: When I turn on Railroads, the middle and east of the map go black with lines. The 'thin gray' lines look black. The pink and blue-gray transcontinental lines are close to the trail colors.
findings.why: I can't see which trail the Union Pacific and Central Pacific follow.
findings.suggestion: Make 'Railroads 1826 to 1911' a lighter, thinner gray, or tell students to turn that sublayer off for step 2 and on again for step 3. Pick transcontinental colors that don't look like any trail color.
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--q4-railroads.png

findings.where: Q4 step 3: clicking a thin gray railroad line
findings.what: I clicked a gray line and it said 'Union Pacific (Transcontinental)'. I thought only the gray ones were other railroads. And what are 'mergers, acquisitions'?
findings.why: I'd think I clicked the wrong line. I'd still write 1869, but I'd be unsure.
findings.suggestion: On the sheet say 'click a thin gray line away from the thick colored ones'. In the pop-up, drop the footnote or say it simply: 'Some railroads changed names, so not every name is known.'
findings.evidence: roads-trails-and-rails-west--q4-grayline.png pop-up: 'Union Pacific (Transcontinental) / Railroad in operation by: 1869 / *Some railroad names aren't recorded due to mergers, acquisitions, and other changes.'

us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850.works: Brown for free and green for slave is a strong split, so the line between them in the East and Missouri sitting north of the dashed line jump out. Every state pop-up has the state's name at the top, and in the bookmark view the town names along the orange routes are big enough to read without zooming further.

findings.where: Q1 'Free states and slave states', step 1: legend, US States and Territories 1850
findings.what: The four groups are at the very bottom of a long legend, and I have to scroll inside it. Under each group there's a long line like 'Free by Compromise of 1820, Missouri Compromise; Acts of Congress admitting Texas, Act of 1848, Ordinance of 1787…'.
findings.why: I'd stop at the first lines and not find the four groups. The long words make me think I have to understand all of it.
findings.suggestion: Use only the four short names as legend labels ('Free state', 'Free by compromise', 'Slave state', 'Slave by compromise') and move the long detail into the pop-ups. Put the states layer at the top of the legend.
findings.evidence: Legend text in us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850--open.png and --q3-slavetrade.png (states group cut off at the bottom of the panel)

findings.where: Q1 step 3: state pop-up (Pennsylvania)
findings.what: It says 1780, then 'Abolition by state action between 1830-1850'. Which year do I write? It never just says 'free state'. It says 'passed legislation against the enslavement of people'.
findings.why: Two different dates confuse me, and I have to work out that 'legislation against the enslavement' means free.
findings.suggestion: Start each pop-up with a plain line: 'Free state: ended slavery by law in 1780' / 'Slave state: joined in 1821'. I'd check Pennsylvania's 'recorded on the primary source as' value, which doesn't fit 1780.
findings.evidence: us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850--q1-pennsylvania.png pop-up: 'This state passed legislation against the enslavement of people 1780. … Abolition by state action between 1830-1850'

findings.where: Q2 'The Missouri Compromise', steps 1–2: clicking the gray dashed Missouri Compromise Line
findings.what: I clicked the dashed line and got 'Unorganized Territory', not the line. There's no '1 of 2'.
findings.why: I'd think I missed and keep clicking. The year 1820 is in there, but I wouldn't be sure it's the answer.
findings.suggestion: Make the line's pop-up open first (draw it on top, or make it easier to hit) and title it 'Missouri Compromise Line, 1820'. Or change the sheet to 'Click just above the line and read the year.'
findings.evidence: us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850--q2-line.png pop-up: 'Unorganized Territory … in 1820 … Free by Missouri Compromise'

findings.where: Q3 'The internal slave trade': legend, Internal Routes of the US Slave Trade
findings.what: The sheet says Amistad and the legend says 'Route of L'Amistead'. The dash-dot, thin dashed and dotted lines all look alike.
findings.why: I'd wonder if it's the same ship, and I can't tell the ship routes from the sea routes.
findings.suggestion: Rename it 'Route of the Amistad'. Give the two ship routes their own color so they stand out from the dotted sea routes.
findings.evidence: Legend text 'Route of L'Amistead'; us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850--q1-pennsylvania.png (dash styles off the coast)

findings.where: Q4 'Routes to freedom', steps 2–3: Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio bookmark
findings.what: The routes go up to Detroit and Lake Erie and then go under the legend or off the edge. I see half a black dot with 'Cha…'. Orange names on the brown states are hard to read, and some names show twice (Chicago, Detroit). I don't know where the Ohio River is.
findings.why: The question is where the routes lead, and I can't see the Canada end.
findings.suggestion: Widen the bookmark to take in Lake Erie and southern Ontario so the black Canada dots show. Give the orange town labels a white halo. On the sheet, say 'the Ohio River is where the brown and green states meet'.
findings.evidence: us-slavery-and-slave-trade-1850--q4-bookmark.png (Canada dot cut at 'Cha', routes running off the right side, double labels)

civil-war-battlefields.works: Blues for the Union and browns for the Confederacy, with the white dashed line, read well at the opening view, and the bigger diamonds make it obvious most fighting was in Virginia. The Gettysburg pop-up is one short sentence with the name in capitals.

findings.where: Q3 'Railroads, North and South', steps 1–3: states layer off, Railroads 1826 to 1863 (static), Boundary between Union and Confederacy
findings.what: I turned the states off like it says, and now I can't see any railroads at all. The white dashed line has almost disappeared on the pale map, so I can't tell north from south.
findings.why: With nothing to compare, I can't answer which side had more railroads.
findings.suggestion: I'd check the railroad layer's visibility range: in the pictures it only draws when zoomed in close. Make it draw at the zoom where both sides fit, make the boundary a dark dashed line, and/or tell students to keep the states on (or make the state fill lighter) instead of turning it off.
findings.evidence: civil-war-battlefields--q3-railroads.png (no railroad lines visible, faint white boundary); railroads only visible zoomed in, in civil-war-battlefields--q4-diamond.png and --q4-gettysburg.png

findings.where: Q1 'A nation divided', step 1: legend, U.S. Civil War States and Territories (1863)
findings.what: The legend shows battles and casualty sizes. The states part is just a heading at the bottom, cut off.
findings.why: I wouldn't know to scroll inside the legend, so I can't match the shades to the groups.
findings.suggestion: Move the states group to the top of the legend, or make the casualty-size key smaller. Or add to the sheet: 'Scroll down in the legend.'
findings.evidence: civil-war-battlefields--open.png and --q2-dc.png (states heading at the bottom of the panel, no swatches showing)

findings.where: Q4 'Where were the battles?', step 2: United States Battlefield Boundaries (Civil War Battlefield Boundary)
findings.what: The sheet says tan areas, but they look pale gray to me. In Virginia the whole state is tan, so they blend in, and big diamonds sit on top of them.
findings.why: I can't find what I'm supposed to click.
findings.suggestion: Give battlefield areas a dark outline and a color the states layer doesn't use, or change the sheet to 'the pale gray shapes'.
findings.evidence: civil-war-battlefields--q4-gettysburg.png and --q4-diamond.png (pale gray-beige shapes, low contrast on tan Virginia); civil-war-battlefields--q2-dc.png

findings.where: Battle diamond pop-up (Antietam), used in Q4
findings.what: The name shows twice, then a red line, then the date in light gray slanted letters, then a broken picture that says 'American Battlefield Trust'.
findings.why: The date is the bit I need and it's the hardest to read.
findings.suggestion: Show the date in dark, regular text and remove or fix the broken image.
findings.evidence: civil-war-battlefields--q4-diamond.png pop-up: 'Antietam / Antietam / ____ / September 16, 1862 – September 18, 1862 / American Battlefield Trust'

findings.where: Legend, Total casualties
findings.what: The smallest size says '< 0'. Less than zero soldiers?
findings.why: It makes me think I'm reading it wrong.
findings.suggestion: I'd check the class breaks and relabel the smallest size (for example '< 10,000').
findings.evidence: Legend text: 'Total casualties … 10,000 … < 0'

findings.where: Q2 'The border states', steps 1–2: zoomed in to Washington, D.C.
findings.what: I see Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, Delaware and District of Columbia written on the map, but not Maryland.
findings.why: The sheet tells me Maryland, but I can't find it on the map to check its shade.
findings.suggestion: Make sure Maryland's name shows at this zoom (it's covered by the diamonds around D.C.).
findings.evidence: civil-war-battlefields--q2-dc.png (no Maryland label); Maryland label only appears closer in, in civil-war-battlefields--q4-diamond.png

the-battle-of-vicksburg.works: The dark pins have bold names, so Grant's route is easy to find and measure, and the opening view shows the whole route plus Jackson. The Port Hudson pop-up gives the start and end dates on one line.

findings.where: Q1 'Why Vicksburg?' and Q2 'Grant's route': The Battle of Vicksburg bookmark
findings.what: The bookmark zooms in so close that Milliken's Bend, Edwards and Jackson are off the screen, and the bottom pin has no name showing. The map was better before I clicked the bookmark.
findings.why: I can't find Jackson or the five pins without zooming back out, and the sheet doesn't tell me to.
findings.suggestion: Set the bookmark to the opening view's extent (Milliken's Bend and Natchez to Jackson).
findings.evidence: the-battle-of-vicksburg--q1-bookmark.png (only Vicksburg, New Carthage, Hard Times and an unnamed pin); the-battle-of-vicksburg--open.png (all pins and Jackson)

findings.where: Q1 step 3: Railroads 1826 to 1911, bookmark zoom
findings.what: There's I-20, Highway 80, Highway 61 and lots of dashed lines. Which one is the railroad? The legend lists Union Pacific and Northern Pacific, but those aren't here.
findings.why: I'd follow a highway or the dashed state line by mistake.
findings.suggestion: Use a basemap without modern highways, or make the railroad darker and thicker. Hide the transcontinental entries from this legend so only the railroad symbol shows.
findings.evidence: the-battle-of-vicksburg--q1-bookmark.png (highways stronger than the railroad); legend text listing transcontinental lines

findings.where: Q3 'The battles of May 1863', steps 1–3: Civil War Battlefields legend and diamonds
findings.what: Here Confederate Victory is gray and Inconclusive is yellow, the same yellow as the Vicksburg pin. The gray diamond looks like the gray 'Other' circle. None of the diamonds have names, so I have to click about eight to find the right ones.
findings.why: I'd mix up who won, and clicking every diamond takes a long time.
findings.suggestion: Use the same colors as the Civil War Battlefields map (brown for Confederate, white for Inconclusive), or change the Vicksburg pin color. Label the May 1863 battles (Port Gibson, Raymond, Jackson, Champion Hill, Big Black River) at this zoom.
findings.evidence: the-battle-of-vicksburg--q3-battles.png legend; the-battle-of-vicksburg--q3-championhill.png (unlabeled diamonds between Bruinsburg Bend and Jackson)

findings.where: Battle pop-ups (Champion Hill, Port Hudson), Q3 and Q4
findings.what: The date is light gray and slanted. There's a broken picture link, and it says 'Tap on image to view page' but there's no image. The top of the box has no name.
findings.why: The date is what I need, and it's the faintest thing in the box.
findings.suggestion: Show the date in dark, regular text, put the battle name in the pop-up header, and remove the broken image and the 'Tap on image' line.
findings.evidence: the-battle-of-vicksburg--q3-championhill.png and --q4-porthudson.png pop-ups: 'May 16, 1863 / Battlefield Trust page / Tap on image to view page'

findings.where: Q4 'Splitting the Confederacy', steps 1, 2 and 4: zoomed out to Port Hudson
findings.what: At this zoom I can't see Memphis, and the only state name I see is Alabama. No Louisiana, Arkansas or Texas. The river is a thin line I can't follow. There are three diamonds by Baton Rouge with no names.
findings.why: I can't say which states are west of the river.
findings.suggestion: Add a 'Memphis to the Gulf' bookmark, and a state-name label layer or a highlighted Mississippi River line. Label Port Hudson. (The pop-up may be covering a state name or two, but Texas and Arkansas aren't showing either.)
findings.evidence: the-battle-of-vicksburg--q4-porthudson.png

findings.where: Q2 step 1: Key Places pin label
findings.what: The map says 'Miliken's Bend' and the sheet says 'Milliken's Bend'.
findings.why: Small, but it makes me check whether it's the same place.
findings.suggestion: Make the pin label 'Milliken's Bend' to match the sheet.
findings.evidence: the-battle-of-vicksburg--open.png label 'Miliken's Bend'
